course.title: Backend Development with Node.js
course.tagline: Build APIs, databases and login systems with Node.js and Express, and deploy a working backend.

days.title: What Node.js Is and How to Install It
days.goal: Explain what Node.js is and run your first Node program.

video.title: Node JS Full Course 2024

steps: Install Node.js LTS from nodejs.org and check node -v and npm -v in the terminal.
Create a folder server-basics and a file app.js.
Write console.log('Hello from Node') and run it with node app.js.
Use process.argv to print a name passed on the command line.
days.task: Run a Node script that prints a greeting using your name from the command line.
days.challenge: Print the current date and your Node version from the same script.

options: A JavaScript runtime that runs outside the browser
quiz.explain: Node.js lets JavaScript run on a server or your computer, not just in a browser.

quiz.q: Which command runs a Node file?
quiz.explain: node followed by the file name executes it.

options: The Node package manager for installing libraries
quiz.explain: npm installs and manages third-party packages for Node projects.

days.title: Modules, require and the File System
days.goal: Split code into modules and read and write files with Node.

video.title: Node.js Full Course 2026

steps: Create a math.js module that exports add and subtract functions.
Import it into app.js with require and use both functions.
Read a text file with fs.readFileSync and print its contents.
Write a new file with fs.writeFileSync containing a log line.
days.task: Build a small script that reads names from a file and writes a greeting for each into another file.
days.challenge: Rewrite the file reading using the async fs.promises version.

quiz.q: How do you share a function from a Node module?
quiz.explain: module.exports exposes values; require() loads them in another file.

options: Reads a file and blocks until it is done
quiz.explain: The Sync version blocks execution until the file is read.

options: Smaller files are easier to read, test and reuse
quiz.explain: Modules keep code organised and reusable.

days.title: npm, package.json and Dependencies
days.goal: Manage a project with npm and install real packages.

video.title: Complete Backend Course | Beginner to Advanced | Node.js, Express, MongoDB

steps: Run npm init -y to create a package.json in your project.
Install express with npm install express and inspect node_modules.
Install nodemon as a dev dependency and add a dev script to package.json.
Run your app with npm run dev and confirm nodemon restarts it on changes.
days.task: Set up a project with package.json, Express installed and a dev script that runs with nodemon.
days.challenge: Install the dotenv package and load a PORT value from a .env file.

quiz.explain: package.json lists the project's name, scripts and installed packages.

quiz.q: What is the difference between dependencies and devDependencies?
options: devDependencies are only needed during development, like testing tools
quiz.explain: Dev tools such as nodemon belong in devDependencies.

options: Installs the packages listed in package.json
quiz.explain: npm install reads package.json and downloads the listed packages.

days.title: Your First HTTP Server with Node
days.goal: Serve responses over HTTP using only Node's built-in modules.

video.title: Learn Node.js and Express with This Free 8-hour Back End Development Course

steps: Create a server with http.createServer that replies 'Hello World'.
Make it listen on port 3000 and visit http://localhost:3000 in a browser.
Read req.url and return a different message for /about.
Set the Content-Type header to application/json and return a JSON object.
days.task: Build a plain Node server with three routes: /, /about and /api/time returning the current time as JSON.
days.challenge: Return a 404 status and message for any unknown route.

options: Makes the server accept requests on port 3000
quiz.explain: listen binds the server to a port so browsers can reach it.

options: Your own computer, addressed by name
quiz.explain: localhost refers to the machine you are working on.

quiz.q: Which header tells the client the response is JSON?
quiz.explain: Content-Type describes the body format being sent.

days.title: Express: Routing and Responses
days.goal: Build a server faster with Express routing.

video.title: Backend Complete Course | NodeJS, ExpressJS, JWT, PostgreSQL, Prisma

steps: Install Express and create an app with app.get for / and /hello.
Return JSON with res.json and a status code with res.status.
Add a route with a parameter, /users/:id, and return the id.
Add a 404 handler at the end of your route list.
days.task: Build an Express server with five routes, including one with a URL parameter.
days.challenge: Add a route that reads a query string like ?search=shoes and echoes it back.

options: A minimal web framework for Node.js
quiz.explain: Express adds routing and helpers on top of Node's HTTP module.

quiz.q: How do you read a route parameter :id in Express?
quiz.explain: Route parameters live in req.params.

options: Sends a JSON response with the right header
quiz.explain: res.json serialises the value and sets the JSON content type.

days.title: Middleware: The Express Pipeline
days.goal: Use middleware to log, parse and protect requests.

video.title: Express.js Crash Course | Build a RESTful API with Middleware in Just 30 Minutes!

steps: Add express.json() so your server can read JSON request bodies.
Write a logger middleware that prints the method and URL of every request.
Write a middleware that blocks requests missing a header and returns 401.
Apply the logger to all routes and the guard to one route only.
days.task: Add logging middleware and JSON body parsing to your server, plus a guard on one route.
days.challenge: Write middleware that measures how long each request takes and logs it.

options: A function that runs during request handling, before or after routes
quiz.explain: Middleware functions run in sequence and can inspect or change requests and responses.

options: Passes control to the next middleware or route
quiz.explain: Calling next() moves the request along the pipeline.

options: To parse JSON request bodies into req.body
quiz.explain: Without it, req.body is undefined for JSON requests.

days.title: Project 1: A Notes REST API
days.goal: Build a complete in-memory REST API for notes.

video.title: Node JS Tutorial | Creation of Rest-Apis with Node and Express.js

steps: Design the routes: GET /notes, GET /notes/:id, POST /notes, PUT /notes/:id, DELETE /notes/:id.
Store notes in an array and give each a unique id.
Validate POST bodies and return 400 when title is missing.
Test every route with curl or Postman.
days.task: Ship a working notes API with all five CRUD routes and validation.
days.challenge: Add a search query ?q= that filters notes by title.

quiz.explain: REST is an architectural style for APIs built on HTTP verbs and resources.

quiz.q: Which HTTP verb creates a resource?
quiz.explain: POST creates; GET reads; PUT updates; DELETE removes.
201 Created is the correct response after a successful POST.

project.title: Notes REST API
project.brief: Build a complete REST API for notes using Express, with in-memory storage, five CRUD routes and validation.
checks: GET, POST, PUT and DELETE routes all work
POST returns 400 when the title is missing
Unknown ids return 404 with a clear message
JSON body parsing is enabled with express.json()
Every route tested with curl or Postman
Code is split into at least two files

days.title: CRUD with Real Data and Validation
days.goal: Make your API robust with validation and proper status codes.

video.title: Build A REST API With Node.js, Express, & MongoDB - Quick

steps: Add validation for every field on create and update.
Return 404 with a clear message when an id does not exist.
Add pagination with ?page= and ?limit= on the list route.
Return consistent JSON shapes for success and error responses.
days.task: Upgrade your notes API with validation, 404 handling and pagination.
days.challenge: Add sorting with ?sort=title or ?sort=created.

quiz.q: Which status code means the resource was not found?
quiz.explain: 404 means the requested resource does not exist.

quiz.q: Why validate input on the server?
options: Clients can send anything, so the server is the last line of defence
quiz.explain: Never trust client input; validate every value server-side.

options: Splitting a long list into pages of results
quiz.explain: Pagination returns a slice of results so clients are not flooded.

days.title: Working with MongoDB and Mongoose
days.goal: Connect Node to MongoDB and model data with Mongoose.

video.title: Express API Tutorial: Introduction

steps: Install mongoose and connect to a local or Atlas MongoDB database.
Define a Note schema with title, body and timestamps.
Replace your in-memory array with database calls.
Test create, read, update and delete against the real database.
days.task: Move your notes API from an array to MongoDB with a Mongoose model.
days.challenge: Add a second model, Category, and link notes to categories by id.

options: An ODM that models MongoDB data in Node.js
quiz.explain: Mongoose adds schemas, validation and helper methods over the MongoDB driver.

options: The shape and rules of a collection's documents
quiz.explain: A schema defines fields, types and validation for documents.

quiz.q: Why use a database instead of an array?
options: Data survives restarts and can grow beyond memory
quiz.explain: In-memory data disappears when the server restarts.

days.title: SQL Databases with PostgreSQL and Prisma
days.goal: Query a relational database from Node with Prisma.

video.title: Express API Tutorial: GET Endpoints

steps: Install Prisma and set up a PostgreSQL database (local or hosted).
Define a Note model in schema.prisma and run a migration.
Use Prisma Client to create and list notes.
Compare the Prisma code with the Mongoose code from yesterday.
days.task: Build a second version of the notes API backed by PostgreSQL through Prisma.
days.challenge: Add a relation so each note belongs to a user.

options: An ORM that generates a typed client for SQL databases
quiz.explain: Prisma lets you query SQL databases with type-safe JavaScript.

options: A versioned change to the database structure
quiz.explain: Migrations track schema changes so databases can be updated safely.

quiz.q: When is SQL a better fit than MongoDB?
options: When data is highly relational and needs strict consistency
quiz.explain: Relational data with joins and transactions suits SQL databases.

days.title: Authentication with JWT
days.goal: Add signup, login and protected routes with JSON Web Tokens.

video.title: Express API Tutorial: Routing Parameters

steps: Install bcryptjs and jsonwebtoken.
Create a User model and a /auth/register route that hashes passwords.
Create a /auth/login route that checks the password and issues a JWT.
Protect the notes routes with middleware that verifies the token.
days.task: Add register, login and a protected route to your API; only logged-in users can manage notes.
days.challenge: Add token expiry of one hour and return a clear error when a token is expired.

options: A signed token that proves who a user is
quiz.explain: A JSON Web Token carries claims and a signature the server can verify.

options: So a stolen database does not expose real passwords
quiz.explain: Hashing is one-way, so leaked hashes cannot be turned back into passwords.

quiz.q: Where should the JWT check happen?
options: In server middleware before protected routes
quiz.explain: The server must verify the token; front-end checks are cosmetic.

days.title: Passwords, Sessions and Security Basics
days.goal: Harden your API against common attacks.

video.title: Express API Tutorial: JSON Request Body

steps: Add rate limiting to the login route.
Sanitise inputs and never log passwords or tokens.
Store secrets in environment variables, never in code.
Add helmet to set secure HTTP headers.
days.task: Audit your API and fix at least five security issues.
days.challenge: Try sending a SQL-injection-style string and a huge payload; confirm the server handles both safely.

quiz.q: Why keep secrets in environment variables?
options: Code in Git history is hard to erase, but env vars stay on the server
quiz.explain: Secrets committed to Git leak; env vars keep them out of the repo.

options: Limits how many requests one client can make in a time window
quiz.explain: Rate limits slow down brute-force and abuse attempts.
Helmet sets headers that reduce common web attacks.

days.title: File Uploads and Serving Files
days.goal: Accept and serve uploaded files with Multer.

video.title: Express API Tutorial: Update and Delete

steps: Install multer and add an upload route for a single image.
Store uploads in an uploads folder with unique file names.
Serve the folder statically with express.static.
Limit file size and accept only image types.
days.task: Add profile-picture upload to your API and return a URL for the uploaded file.
days.challenge: Add an endpoint that lists all uploaded file names and sizes.

options: Middleware that handles multipart file uploads in Express
quiz.explain: Multer parses multipart/form-data and saves uploaded files.

options: To avoid collisions and path tricks from user-supplied names
quiz.explain: User file names can collide or contain dangerous paths.

options: Serves files from a folder over HTTP
quiz.explain: express.static serves files like images from a directory.

days.title: Project 2: Task Manager API with Auth
days.goal: Combine everything so far into a full task manager API.

video.title: Node JS Full Course 2024

steps: Design the data model: users, tasks with title, status and due date.
Build auth routes and protect all task routes.
Implement full CRUD with validation, filtering and pagination.
Write a README documenting every endpoint.
days.task: Ship a documented task manager API with auth, CRUD, filtering and pagination.
days.challenge: Add a route that returns task counts by status.

options: Endpoints, methods, request bodies, responses and errors
quiz.explain: Good docs let another developer use the API without reading its code.

options: Users must only see their own data
quiz.explain: Scoping data to the owner is a core security rule.

options: It covers its use cases with correct auth, validation and docs
quiz.explain: Completeness means the promised features work correctly and safely.

project.title: Task Manager API with Auth
project.brief: Build a task manager API with user registration, JWT login, protected routes and full task CRUD with filtering and pagination.
checks: Register and login issue a valid JWT
Task routes reject requests without a token
Tasks are scoped to the logged-in user
List supports filtering and pagination
Validation errors return 400 with a message
README documents every endpoint

days.title: Testing Your API with Jest and Supertest
days.goal: Write automated tests for your routes.

video.title: Node.js Full Course 2026

steps: Install jest and supertest as dev dependencies.
Write a test that GET /notes returns 200 and an array.
Write a test that POST with a missing title returns 400.
Run the tests with npm test and make them all pass.
days.task: Write at least six passing tests covering your main routes and error cases.
days.challenge: Add a test that a protected route returns 401 without a token.

options: Makes HTTP requests to your Express app in tests
quiz.explain: Supertest lets tests call your app like a real client.

options: They catch regressions and prove the API behaves as expected
quiz.explain: Tests give confidence that changes do not break existing behaviour.

options: A check that an actual value matches the expected value
quiz.explain: Assertions compare actual results with expected results.

days.title: Error Handling and Logging
days.goal: Handle errors cleanly and log what matters.

video.title: Complete Backend Course | Beginner to Advanced | Node.js, Express, MongoDB

steps: Add a central error-handling middleware that returns consistent JSON.
Use try/catch in async routes or an async wrapper.
Add a logger (morgan or winston) that records requests and errors.
Make sure no stack traces leak to clients in production.
days.task: Refactor your API so every error flows through one handler with clean JSON responses.
days.challenge: Add a request-id to each log line so one request can be traced.

quiz.q: What is a central error handler?
options: One middleware that catches errors from all routes
quiz.explain: Central handling keeps error responses consistent and code clean.

quiz.q: Why hide stack traces from clients?
options: They reveal server internals attackers can use
quiz.explain: Stack traces leak file paths and library details.

options: Requests, errors and key events — never secrets
quiz.explain: Logs should help debugging without exposing sensitive data.

days.title: Environment Config and Deployment Prep
days.goal: Prepare your API for a real server.

video.title: Learn Node.js and Express with This Free 8-hour Back End Development Course

steps: Move all config (port, database URL, JWT secret) into environment variables.
Add a .gitignore that excludes node_modules and .env.
Create a production start script and test it locally.
Check the app starts with NODE_ENV=production.
days.task: Make your API fully configurable by environment variables with no secrets in code.
days.challenge: Write a DEPLOY.md checklist for taking the API live.

options: node_modules, .env and other generated or secret files
quiz.explain: Generated files and secrets must never be committed.

options: An environment variable that tells the app which mode it is in
quiz.explain: NODE_ENV switches behaviour between development and production.

options: It gives one standard command to run the app anywhere
quiz.explain: A start script documents how the app runs in production.

days.title: Deploying to Render or Railway
days.goal: Deploy your API so anyone can call it.

video.title: Backend Complete Course | NodeJS, ExpressJS, JWT, PostgreSQL, Prisma

steps: Create a free account on Render or Railway.
Connect your GitHub repository and set the build and start commands.
Add your environment variables in the hosting dashboard.
Test the live URL with curl and fix any deployment errors.
days.task: Deploy your task manager API live and verify every route on the public URL.
days.challenge: Set up automatic deploys so every push to main goes live.

quiz.q: What does a hosting platform need to run your app?
options: The code, a start command and environment variables
quiz.explain: The platform needs to know how to start the app and what config to give it.

quiz.q: Why do deploys fail most often?
options: Missing environment variables or a wrong start command
quiz.explain: Missing env vars and wrong start commands are the classic deploy failures.

quiz.q: What is a health check endpoint?
options: A simple route like /health that proves the app is running
quiz.explain: Platforms ping a health endpoint to know the app is alive.

days.title: Caching, Rate Limits and Scaling Basics
days.goal: Make your API faster and more resilient.

video.title: Express.js Crash Course | Build a RESTful API with Middleware in Just 30 Minutes!

steps: Add in-memory caching for a slow list endpoint.
Add rate limiting to all routes.
Add compression middleware to shrink responses.
Measure response times before and after caching.
days.task: Add caching, compression and rate limiting to your API and record the speed difference.
days.challenge: Cache a single resource by id and invalidate it when the resource updates.

options: Stores a computed result so later requests skip the work
quiz.explain: Caching trades a little memory for much faster repeated responses.

quiz.q: When must a cache be invalidated?
options: When the underlying data changes, or clients see stale results
quiz.explain: Stale cache entries lie to clients after the data changes.

options: Shrinks response bodies so they travel faster
quiz.explain: Compression reduces the bytes sent over the network.

days.title: WebSockets and Real-Time Updates
days.goal: Add live updates with Socket.io.

video.title: Node JS Tutorial | Creation of Rest-Apis with Node and Express.js

steps: Install socket.io and attach it to your HTTP server.
Emit an event whenever a task is created or updated.
Build a tiny HTML page that connects and shows live updates.
Broadcast the event to all connected clients except the sender.
days.task: Add a live feed to your task API so new tasks appear instantly on a connected page.
days.challenge: Add a 'user is typing' style event to the demo page.

options: A persistent two-way connection between client and server
quiz.explain: WebSockets stay open so either side can push messages at any time.

quiz.q: When are WebSockets better than polling?
options: When updates must arrive instantly without constant requests
quiz.explain: Polling wastes requests; WebSockets push only when something happens.

options: Sends an event to a connected client
quiz.explain: emit sends a named event with data to a socket.

days.title: Project 3: Blog API with Comments
days.goal: Build a full blog API with posts, comments and likes.

video.title: Build A REST API With Node.js, Express, & MongoDB - Quick

steps: Design models for users, posts and comments.
Build CRUD for posts and nested routes for comments.
Add likes and a route that returns the most-liked posts.
Document the API and write tests for the main flows.
days.task: Ship a blog API with posts, comments, likes and tests.
days.challenge: Add pagination and search to the posts list.

quiz.q: How should comments relate to posts?
options: Each comment stores the post id it belongs to
quiz.explain: A reference from comment to post keeps the data linked and queryable.

options: A route like /posts/:id/comments that belongs under a parent resource
quiz.explain: Nested routes express ownership: comments live under a post.

quiz.q: Why add search to a list endpoint?
options: Clients need to find content without downloading everything
quiz.explain: Search keeps list endpoints useful as data grows.

project.title: Blog API with Comments
project.brief: Build a blog API with posts, nested comments, likes, search and pagination, backed by a real database.
checks: Posts support full CRUD
Comments are nested under posts
Like endpoint works and most-liked list is available
Search and pagination work on the posts list
At least four tests pass
API is documented in a README or Swagger

days.title: API Documentation with Swagger
days.goal: Document your API so others can use it.

video.title: Express API Tutorial: Introduction

steps: Install swagger-ui-express and swagger-jsdoc.
Annotate your routes with OpenAPI comments.
Serve the docs at /api-docs and open them in a browser.
Test an endpoint from the Swagger UI.
days.task: Publish interactive Swagger docs for your blog API.
days.challenge: Add request examples and error responses to every endpoint doc.

options: A standard for describing REST APIs, with an interactive docs UI
quiz.explain: OpenAPI describes endpoints so tools can generate docs and clients.

options: Other developers can use it without reading your code
quiz.explain: Docs are the contract between the API and its users.

quiz.q: What can you do in Swagger UI?
options: Try endpoints live from the browser
quiz.explain: Swagger UI lets you send real requests to the documented endpoints.

days.title: Background Jobs and Queues
days.goal: Run slow work in the background instead of blocking requests.

video.title: Express API Tutorial: GET Endpoints

steps: Identify a slow task in your API, like sending a welcome email.
Install BullMQ or a simple in-memory queue.
Move the slow task into a job that runs after the response.
Add a route that shows the job queue status.
days.task: Move email sending (simulated by a log) into a background job in your API.
days.challenge: Add retry logic so a failed job runs again up to three times.

options: Slow work should not block the HTTP response
quiz.explain: Responses should return fast; heavy work runs afterwards.

options: A list of jobs processed one by one by workers
quiz.explain: Queues hold jobs until a worker picks them up.

options: Transient failures like a down service often succeed on a retry
quiz.explain: Retries handle temporary outages without losing work.

days.title: Monitoring, Uptime and Alerts
days.goal: Know when your API is down before your users tell you.

video.title: Express API Tutorial: Routing Parameters

steps: Add a /health endpoint that checks the database connection.
Log errors with enough context to diagnose them.
Sign up for a free uptime monitor and point it at your API.
Create an alert that notifies you when the API stops responding.
days.task: Set up health checks and an uptime monitor for your live API.
days.challenge: Write a runbook: what to check first when the API returns 500s.

quiz.q: What does a health endpoint check?
options: Whether the app and its database are actually working
quiz.explain: A health check proves the app can serve real requests.

options: You learn about outages before users complain
quiz.explain: Monitoring turns silent failures into alerts you can act on.

options: Written steps for diagnosing and fixing common incidents
quiz.explain: A runbook makes incident response calm and repeatable.

days.title: Refactoring and Code Organisation
days.goal: Clean up your API into a professional structure.

video.title: Express API Tutorial: JSON Request Body

steps: Split routes, controllers and models into separate folders.
Move repeated validation into shared middleware.
Remove dead code and duplicated logic.
Run your tests after each change to prove nothing broke.
days.task: Refactor your blog API into routes/controllers/models folders with all tests still passing.
days.challenge: Extract one piece of logic into a reusable service module.

options: Improving code structure without changing what it does
quiz.explain: Refactoring makes code cleaner while behaviour stays the same.

options: Routes describe URLs; controllers hold the logic, so each is easier to change
quiz.explain: Separation of concerns keeps files small and focused.

quiz.q: How do you know a refactor is safe?
options: Tests still pass and behaviour is unchanged
quiz.explain: Passing tests prove the refactor did not break behaviour.

days.title: Capstone Planning: A Real Backend Service
days.goal: Plan a complete backend service you will build and deploy.

video.title: Express API Tutorial: Update and Delete

steps: Choose a service: a shop API, a booking API or a social API.
List the resources, endpoints and data models.
Decide the auth model and which routes are protected.
Sketch the database schema on paper.
days.task: Write a full capstone plan with endpoints, models, auth rules and a build order.
days.challenge: Cut the scope to what you can build and test in two days.

quiz.q: What should a capstone plan include?
options: Resources, endpoints, models, auth and a build order
quiz.explain: A plan maps the whole service before a line of code is written.

quiz.q: Why decide auth rules up front?
options: Auth mistakes are expensive to fix after routes are built
quiz.explain: Designing auth early prevents data leaks later.

quiz.q: How do you choose a capstone idea?
options: Pick something useful with clear data and clear users
quiz.explain: A useful, well-scoped idea is finishable and demonstrable.

days.title: Capstone Build: Models and Auth
days.goal: Build the data layer and authentication for your capstone service.

video.title: Node JS Full Course 2024

steps: Create the project, connect the database and define all models.
Implement register and login with hashed passwords and JWT.
Protect the routes that need a logged-in user.
Seed the database with realistic sample data.
days.task: Ship the capstone data layer and auth, with seed data you can test against.
days.challenge: Add a role field so some routes are admin-only.

options: Realistic sample records used for development and demos
quiz.explain: Seed data lets you test and demo without creating records by hand.

options: So a database leak does not expose real passwords
quiz.explain: Hashing is one-way, so stolen hashes are useless to attackers.

options: Permissions depend on the user's role, like admin or customer
quiz.explain: Roles restrict sensitive actions to the right users.

days.title: Capstone Build: Core Endpoints
days.goal: Build the main features of your capstone service.

video.title: Node.js Full Course 2026

steps: Implement CRUD for your main resource with validation.
Add filtering, search and pagination to list endpoints.
Implement the second resource and its relationship to the first.
Test every endpoint with Postman or curl.
days.task: Ship the capstone core endpoints with validation, filtering and pagination.
days.challenge: Add one endpoint that aggregates data, like totals or counts.

quiz.q: What does an aggregate endpoint do?
options: Combines many records into a summary, like a total
quiz.explain: Aggregations turn raw records into useful numbers.

options: Every endpoint is an entry point an attacker can abuse
quiz.explain: Unvalidated endpoints are the most common API vulnerability.

quiz.q: How do you test an endpoint?
options: Send real requests and check the status and body
quiz.explain: Real requests prove the endpoint works end to end.

days.title: Capstone Build: Polish, Tests and Docs
days.goal: Finish the capstone with tests, docs and deployment.

video.title: Complete Backend Course | Beginner to Advanced | Node.js, Express, MongoDB

steps: Write tests for the main flows and make them pass.
Add Swagger docs for every endpoint.
Add error handling, logging and a health endpoint.
Deploy the service and verify the live URL.
days.task: Ship the finished capstone: tested, documented and deployed live.
days.challenge: Record a short walkthrough of the API using the Swagger UI.

quiz.q: What proves a backend capstone is done?
options: It is tested, documented, deployed and meets its plan
quiz.explain: Done means working, proven by tests, documented and live.

options: Docs written late are usually wrong or missing
quiz.explain: Writing docs while building keeps them accurate.

quiz.q: What is the best next step after this course?
options: Build a front-end for your API or learn TypeScript and testing in depth
quiz.explain: A front-end on your own API is the natural next step.

days.title: Demo Day: Present Your API
days.goal: Present your capstone API clearly and plan what to learn next.

video.title: Learn Node.js and Express with This Free 8-hour Back End Development Course

steps: Write a one-page README summary: what the API does and how to run it.
Record or write a 2-minute demo showing register, login and one full CRUD flow.
Ask one person to follow your README and call your live API.
List three things you would improve and the next technology you want to learn.
days.task: Publish your capstone README and demo, and share the live API link with one person.
days.challenge: Fix the first problem your tester finds, then redeploy.

quiz.q: Why demo your API to someone else?

capstone.title: A Complete Backend Service, Deployed
capstone.brief: Design, build, test, document and deploy a complete backend service of your choice — for example a shop API, a booking API or a social API. It must have user auth with JWT, at least two related resources with full CRUD, validation, pagination, tests and Swagger docs, running live on a public URL.
checks: Service is deployed live and responds on a public URL
Auth works: register, login and protected routes
At least two related resources with full CRUD
Validation returns clear 400 errors
List endpoints support pagination
At least six automated tests pass
Swagger docs cover every endpoint
deliverables: GitHub repository with the full source code
A Postman collection or curl examples for every endpoint
A short written summary of the architecture and what you learned
